methods.label: Compare the distance expressions
methods.explanation:
We do not need Ian's time and speed separately. Comparing distances will reveal a combination of them that also determines Jan's extra distance.

Let Ian drive for \(t>0\) hours at an average speed of \(v>0\) miles per hour. His distance is \(tv\). Han's time and speed are \(t+1\) and \(v+5\), so Han's extra distance is
\[
(t+1)(v+5)-tv
=5t+v+5.
\]
This equals \(70\), giving
\[
5t+v=65.
\]
Jan's time and speed are \(t+2\) and \(v+10\). His extra distance is therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
(t+2)(v+10)-tv
&=10t+2v+20\\
&=2(5t+v)+20\\
&=2\cdot65+20\\
&=150.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus Jan drove \(\boxed{150}\) miles more than Ian, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
